components.label: The latch and the arteriole record
components.note: The latch-bridge state is textbook in conduit arteries (VASO-C010: VASO-E003) but not generic across vascular smooth muscle — present in a parent artery, absent one branch order down (VASO-E021). Where the thesis needs it, the record points away: pressurized skeletal-muscle arterioles show maintained or rising phosphorylation (VASO-C020: VASO-E020), no arteriole holding cost has been measured (VASO-E019), and no study identifies a latch at a tender point (VASO-E016); the Doppler-resistance reading (VASO-E027) is co-explained by contracture. Densification's reversibility (VASO-C077) is anchor-only, with no record behind it.

components.label: The breath as key, and the speed of release
components.note: Slow breathing shifts autonomic balance globally (VASO-C013: VASO-E009). The felt seconds-scale release rests on proponent testimony (VASO-C004: VASO-E014). The two-key necessity (VASO-C039) has one admitted record, VASO-E067, establishing only that a published pressure-only protocol carried no breathing instruction; the state-not-structure inference (VASO-C011) rests on priors, with VASO-E030 (changes over visits after needling) as context and VASO-E035 as the argument itself. The blood-first ordering (VASO-C073) is anchor-only. Attention can regulate a peripheral vascular bed without arousal (VASO-C006: VASO-E008), by a vagal immune route over minutes (VASO-E041). No time-resolved record exists in either direction.

components.label: Vascular tension as memory participating in mind
components.note: Vascular state can modulate neurons instantaneously in rat brain (VASO-C012: VASO-E005; the hypothesis stated, VASO-E004). The memory attribution (VASO-C021) rests on hypothesis statements (VASO-E013, VASO-E038) and fails the write–store–read criteria (VASO-E017). The composite three-element hold of the perforator account (VASO-C174) is held on an anchor in an unread source. Presently untested rather than contradicted.

components.label: The contemplative maps
components.note: The only record on VASO-C022 is the founding essay's uncited assertion about where the traditional maps place the knots (VASO-E039). No blinded coding against chance has been done; the perforator essay's sharper correspondence is catalogued, not evidenced.

researchPriority.reason: The central crux — whether anything objective happens locally within seconds of an exhale, and whether the breath is a key at all — is decidable by two small studies (VASO-R001, VASO-R020) that cost less than a mid-size grant, and the ledger now holds a pressure-only protocol that a breath-randomized repeat could turn into a direct test. Either result would move the case verdict; nothing in the current record can.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The claim is held on hypothesis statements (VASO-E013, VASO-E038) that carry no evidential weight, and its one substantive record, VASO-E017, qualifies it: a hysteretic state is not a memory until it depends on prior input, can be read out, and discriminates between inputs, and the latch literature addresses none of these. The read path (VASO-C012) and the latch (VASO-C010) are real but supply only the necessary pieces.

treatment.plainLanguage: Blood vessels, by holding tension, may store something like predictions or 'clinging' that the mind then reads back.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If demonstrated it would be a new biological memory mechanism; nothing in the ledger bears on it in either direction, so it currently decides nothing.
treatment.strongestObjection: A thermostat has hysteresis without an autobiography; the nearest real write–store–read loop in a flow network is a slime mold's tubes, not a mammal's arteries.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: An animal preparation in which different induced vascular states bias later neural responses under identical stimulation with oxygenation clamped (VASO-R005).
A demonstration that erasing a vascular state selectively erases or relaxes a specific neural representation.
A clean negative in VASO-R005 — vascular effects that track only instantaneous perfusion — would move the claim to contradicted.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The report's audit finds no study identifying a smooth-muscle latch at any tender point (VASO-E016). The arteriole compartment has been examined and shows maintained or rising phosphorylation, not an economical hold (VASO-E020), and no arteriole's holding cost has been measured (VASO-E019). The Doppler resistance pattern near trigger points (VASO-E027) is co-explained by contracture compression by the source's own authors and is weighed at zero diagnosticity. VASO-E037 is the hypothesis stated by its proponent; the second-essay records rest on an unread source and are treated as absent. State-not-scar is shared by all three accounts; the vascular attribution is what is unevidenced.

treatment.plainLanguage: A knot is a small vessel inside the muscle held shut by a low-energy smooth-muscle latch, starving its neighborhood, with guarding layered on top.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If true it decides the case for the vascular account; the ledger's only compartment-specific records lean against it without refuting it.
treatment.strongestObjection: Every direct measurement in pressurized skeletal-muscle arterioles shows sustained activation, the opposite of a latch signature, and the abnormal Doppler sits in conduit-scale vessels the imaging authors explain by contracture.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A pressurized skeletal-muscle arteriole holding constriction after stimulus withdrawal at falling phosphorylation and measured low energetic cost (VASO-R004).
A palpated knot stiff on elastography, active on EMG and metabolically cold on FDG-PET (VASO-R013).
Time-resolved imaging showing perfusion rising before stiffness falls at a release (VASO-R001).
Against it: the non-latching phenotype throughout skeletal-muscle arterioles, or a hot knot on PET.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone, in a source (SRC-JHONG-2026A) the ledger has not been able to read and verify; no admitted evidence record bears on it. Its three elements — vessel tone, hyaluronan collar, fascial tether — are each stated as propositions, none measured at a tender point.

treatment.plainLanguage: On the perforator picture, what holds a knot is three things at once — the vessel's tone, a gelled collar around the bundle, and the tether it makes with the fascial sheet.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: It is the mechanism of a genuinely different account with cheap tests; with no record behind it, it neither adds nor subtracts from the case.
treatment.strongestObjection: The stiff regions blinded sonographers map lie inside the muscle, not in the fascia under the skin, and the account's only source is an unread, AI-generated essay.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Blinded tender points coinciding with pencil-Doppler perforators above chance (VASO-R015).
A knot released by saline hydrodissection at its perforator with no breath (VASO-R017).
Pressure during an inhale-and-hold failing to clear points that pressure during exhalation clears (VASO-R016, VASO-R020).
Against it: coincidence at chance, or no effect of hydrodissection.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The only record is the founding essay's uncited assertion that the traditional maps place the knots along the midline and limbs (VASO-E039), with no coding rule and no chance baseline. No primary text or anatomical comparison has been admitted.

treatment.plainLanguage: The Tibetan, Indian and Chinese maps of bodily knots and channels are early first-person observations of the same vascular tension system.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Even a genuine alignment with vascular geography would not show that anything latches or clenches; a null would retire the convergence argument only.
treatment.strongestObjection: Correspondence found after the fact is post-hoc matching until coded blind against chance.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Preregistered anatomical coding of rtsa mdud, granthi and ashi locations aligning with vascular, autonomic or fascial landmarks above chance (VASO-R006).
The same coding finding alignment at chance.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Hai and Murphy's kinetic model reproduces high sustained stress at low phosphorylation in smooth-muscle preparations (VASO-E003, strong). The case's own study qualifies the capability as non-generic: present in a parent artery, absent in its own downstream branch, never followed into arterioles (VASO-E021). VASO-E034 overstates the model and carries no weight.

treatment.plainLanguage: Smooth muscle in vessel walls can hold tension cheaply after the signal that started it has faded — the latch-bridge state.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Textbook physiology every account accepts; it establishes that the mechanism exists somewhere, not that it operates where a knot would need it.
treatment.strongestObjection: Latch behaviour depends on vessel type and motor-protein phenotype, and the one paired comparison lost it one branch order downstream.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A paired-caliber study showing latch capacity persists into skeletal-muscle arterioles under stimulus withdrawal (VASO-R004) would raise its diagnosticity.
A study showing the non-latching phenotype throughout resistance vessels would confine the claim to conduit arteries.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The claim is a conditional inference and is graded on physiological priors: remodeling takes days to weeks, so a seconds-scale objective release would be a change of state. Its records are the argument itself (VASO-E035) and a pilot in which needled points shrank over visits (VASO-E030, context), neither of which films seconds. Its premise — an objective local event within seconds — is the unmeasured crux.

treatment.plainLanguage: If a knot really releases in seconds, what released was something the body was doing, not damaged tissue.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Separates state from scar but not vessel from guarding or densification, all of which are states.
treatment.strongestObjection: The antecedent has never been measured, and 'state' includes motor guarding and fascial densification, so satisfying it does not favour the vascular accounts.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Time-resolved elastography showing a stiffness drop within seconds of a felt release at palpated but not sham sites (VASO-R001).
Felt releases with no reproducible local transition would leave the conditional true but idle.
A demonstrated structural change on a seconds timescale would break the inference.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor in the founding essay with no admitted evidence record; the Stecco-group primaries and the reversal timescale have not been retrieved (VASO-R008).

treatment.plainLanguage: The gluey hyaluronan between fascial layers can thin again under pressure, movement and warmth.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If densification reverses within a session, the knot can be a fast-reversing state without any vessel — a direct non-vascular competitor.
treatment.strongestObjection: No record gives the timescale of hyaluronan viscosity change under load or warmth.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A retrieved primary showing hyaluronan densification reversing within minutes under pressure or warmth.
Time-resolved imaging showing stiffness dropping with no perfusion change.
A retrieved timescale of hours would remove densification as a candidate for the seconds-scale release.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Blood-pressure pulsations modulate central neurons through mechanosensitive channels in rat preparations and awake animals (VASO-E005, strong). The hypothesis paper (VASO-E004) proposes but demonstrates nothing. The demonstration is of instantaneous modulation in brain, not storage or peripheral readout.

treatment.plainLanguage: The state of nearby blood vessels can change what neurons do.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Necessary for vasocomputation but consistent with ordinary neurovascular physiology; it shows vessels can nudge neurons now, not store anything.
treatment.strongestObjection: Rat brain, rapid timescale, no history dependence — a read path without a store.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Peripheral sensory endings shown to respond to arteriolar caliber changes in tissue.
History-dependent neural readout of vascular state with oxygenation clamped (VASO-R005).

claimAssessments.reasoning: A systematic review documents reproducible rises in heart-rate variability and respiratory sinus arrhythmia during slow breathing in healthy humans (VASO-E009, strong). VASO-E036 is an uncited restatement at zero weight. The measure is global and cardiac; no local tissue effect is recorded.

treatment.plainLanguage: Breathing slowly, especially with long exhalations, reliably tilts the nervous system toward its rest-and-digest side.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Every account accepts a global autonomic shift; the site-specific unlatching the thesis adds is what has never been measured.
treatment.strongestObjection: A heart-rate measure in people with no tender point in the study says nothing about a vessel at a knot.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A local perfusion or stiffness change at a knot time-locked to the exhale and absent at sham sites would raise its diagnosticity.
Equal clearance under held breath and slow exhalation would confine its relevance to the global shift.

claimAssessments.reasoning: A systematic review finds manual examination for trigger points not demonstrated reliable or valid, with no reference standard (VASO-E011, strong); the Quintner critique contests the construct (VASO-E010); proponent groups concede the point (VASO-E029) and state it in their own words, reporting imaging confirmed 71.5% of palpated spots (VASO-E078, VASO-E079, VASO-E081; VASO-E080 context).

treatment.plainLanguage: Examiners do not reliably agree on where trigger points are, there is no agreed test for what one is, and the construct itself is disputed.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: It weakens the observation base of every account equally, and requires any decisive experiment to fix its sites by instrument.
treatment.strongestObjection: Imaging-anchored localization escapes the manual-exam problem, and imaging confirmed about three-quarters of one examiner's spots.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A demonstrated inter-examiner reliability study with an instrumented reference standard.
A census with pain-free controls in which imaging fails to pick out palpated spots would strengthen the critique further.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The first population record: two people reporting no pain had eleven or more tender points at the eighteen fixed sites (VASO-E082, weak), in a pain-selected sample (VASO-E083 context). The reliability critique reaches the observation itself (VASO-E012). A second-hand prevalence figure (VASO-E028) and the essay's report (VASO-E015) add near-zero weight; VASO-E018 concerns feasibility only.

treatment.plainLanguage: Small, sharply tender spots are common in ordinary people's muscles.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: All accounts start from it; its truth decides nothing between them.
treatment.strongestObjection: The one population survey is pain-selected and tests fixed sites rather than counting palpable knots, and whether the spots are reliably identifiable is itself disputed.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A knot census with blinded examiners, pressure algometry and imaging in an unselected sample (VASO-R002, VASO-R010).
Blinded examiners failing to find reproducible points in pain-free adults would undermine it.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Sustained spontaneous activity was found in the nidus of every trigger point and not in adjacent non-tender fibers (VASO-E001), but endplate noise also appears at four of eleven non-tender endplate-zone sites and never off the zone (VASO-E031), so the signature is a prevalence gradient. VASO-E043 is derivative; VASO-E052 rests on an unread source.

treatment.plainLanguage: Trigger points hum with electrical activity more often than nearby non-tender spots in the same nerve-supply zone, and never where there is no such zone.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Shows the knot is electrically maintained — state, not scar — but the signal is skeletal-muscle electrophysiology living in the endplate zone, which fits guarding as well as any vascular account.
treatment.strongestObjection: The signature tracks the endplate zone first and the trigger point second; the silent controls may simply have lain off the zone.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A repeat with matched endplate-zone controls (VASO-R011).
Sympathetic blockade quieting the nidus (VASO-R009, VASO-R012) would tie it to autonomic drive.

claimAssessments.reasoning: One record: mental arithmetic raised trigger-point EMG while control sites in the same muscle stayed comparatively quiet, in fourteen subjects, one lineage (VASO-E002). VASO-E033 restates it. The control needle was not placed in a matched endplate-zone site, so selectivity for the trigger point over any endplate is open.

treatment.plainLanguage: Doing arithmetic in your head turns up the electrical activity inside a tender point but not a centimeter away.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Shows the brain can write to the point — the write half of any storage account — but three readings (stress-sensitive endplates, a sympathetic write to an arteriole, a skin-territory vasoconstriction) fit it equally.
treatment.strongestObjection: Small, old, unreplicated, no vascular measurement, and the control site may have been off the endplate zone.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Selective rise at the trigger point with a quiet matched endplate-zone control (VASO-R011).
A comparable rise at the control would relocate the effect to stress-sensitive endplates generally.
A skin-perfusion fall over the point and not over control skin during the task.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone in an unread source (SRC-JHONG-2026A); no admitted evidence record. The needle in McNulty 1994 recorded muscle, not skin, so nothing in the ledger bears on a cutaneous write.

treatment.plainLanguage: The stress-induced rise at a trigger point is really the brain narrowing skin vessels over that spot, the way it makes a face blush or blanch.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If true it would locate the write in the perforator bed and give the addressability claim an ordinary mechanism; with no record it decides nothing.
treatment.strongestObjection: The recorded signal was intramuscular EMG; no skin perfusion was measured at any trigger point under a stressor.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A localized fall in skin perfusion over the tender point and not over control skin during mental arithmetic (laser speckle).
Global or absent skin-perfusion changes under the same task.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Supported only by first-person and practitioner testimony from the hypothesis's proponent, in an AI-generated essay (VASO-E014, weak). Consistent with widespread lore, contradicted by no one, measured by no one. It is evidence that people feel a release, not that anything happens in the tissue.

treatment.plainLanguage: Press into a knot and breathe out slowly, and within seconds something feels like it lets go.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The anchor phenomenon of the case, but a felt release fits expectation and interpretation as well as any tissue event.
treatment.strongestObjection: Expectation and attention cannot be excluded from any first-person release report, and the one pressure-only protocol in the ledger cleared imaged points with no breath instruction.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Time-locked stiffness and perfusion transitions at the felt release, exceeding sham and pressure-alone controls (VASO-R001).
Felt releases with no reproducible local transition would leave it a percept.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The one admitted record (VASO-E067, context) establishes that a published pressure-only protocol carried no breathing instruction, recording or manipulation — and nothing more. What that protocol achieved is recorded against the active/latent question on VASO-C005, over minutes, and is not spent here as a grade. Breathing was neither instructed nor held constant, so 'no breath instruction' is not 'breath excluded'. The claim remains held on its proponent's anchor.

treatment.plainLanguage: Pressure alone, without the breath, does not release a knot.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Whether the breath is a necessary key separates 'breath necessary', 'breath gating' and 'breath irrelevant' — and with it the cleanest argument that the releasing element answers to autonomic state.
treatment.strongestObjection: A pressure-only protocol with nobody told how to breathe made most imaged trigger points undetectable within a session.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A breath-randomized repeat in which pressure during an inhale-and-hold clears no fewer points than free breathing (VASO-R020) — the claim would fail.
Inhale-and-hold blocking clearance while slow exhalation matches or beats free breathing — the claim would gain support.
Release by hydrodissection with no breath (VASO-R017) would refute necessity.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone; no admitted evidence record. The runners' study performed no Doppler and archived no cine loops, and the trapezius pilot measured changes over visits, so the order of perfusion and stiffness change has never been observed anywhere.

treatment.plainLanguage: When a knot releases with the breath, blood should return first and the stiffness should drop second.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A timing prediction both vascular accounts make and neither guarding nor densification makes; it is the cheapest discriminating signature in the case.
treatment.strongestObjection: No time-resolved measurement exists in either direction.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Perfusion rising before stiffness falls across release events (VASO-R001, VASO-R016).
Stiffness leading, or the two simultaneous, or stiffness dropping with no perfusion change.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Supported by biochemistry (VASO-E006), a second-hand review (VASO-E007), Doppler (VASO-E022), and the trapezius stiff-area gradient — active and latent areas above normal (VASO-E091), the normal-site value (VASO-E090), classifiers (VASO-E096, VASO-E099) and overall ROC separation (VASO-E100, VASO-E102), with VASO-E088, VASO-E097, VASO-E101 and VASO-E103 as context. Qualified by no pain-free controls (VASO-E026), non-classifying flow indices (VASO-E025) and the calf active-versus-latent comparison lacking control tissue (VASO-E070; VASO-E068, VASO-E069, VASO-E071, VASO-E072 context). VASO-E042 is interpretation; VASO-E050 and VASO-E051 rest on an unread source.

treatment.plainLanguage: The spots examiners call trigger points are chemically, mechanically and hemodynamically different from surrounding muscle at group level.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Real differences, but every account predicts them; nothing here says what the stiff tissue is.
treatment.strongestObjection: Every comparison sits inside symptomatic muscle at palpation-selected sites, from one NIH lineage for biochemistry and trapezius imaging, with no pain-free baseline.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A census with pain-free controls and instrument-fixed sites replicating the stiffness and flow differences.
The same census finding that stiffness and Doppler measures do not pick out palpated spots.

claimAssessments.reasoning: A preregistered within-subject study in 57 volunteers found attention toward the inflamed site produced smaller, faster-resolving responses with no arousal difference (VASO-E008, strong, single lab). The route is vagal immune regulation over tens of minutes, in skin the parasympathetic system does not directly innervate (VASO-E041).

treatment.plainLanguage: Paying attention to an inflamed patch of skin makes the inflammation smaller and shorter, without any change in stress arousal.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: An existence proof that cognition can write to a peripheral bed at a chosen site; it says nothing about knots, smooth muscle or seconds.
treatment.strongestObjection: Minutes-scale immune regulation by a vagal route is not a latch release.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Independent replication.
A demonstration that directed attention changes smooth-muscle tone at a chosen site on a seconds timescale would raise its diagnosticity.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Median pulsatility index 8.3 near active sites against 3.0 near normal sites, P<.05 (VASO-E022), in conduit-scale arteries; qualified by no pain-free control group (VASO-E026) and by the source's own finding that the index could not classify sites.

treatment.plainLanguage: Arteries near active trigger points show flow that surges and falls more sharply with each heartbeat than arteries near normal sites.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Compatible with distal constriction, contracture compressing the bed, inflammation or transducer pressure — the authors list all four.
treatment.strongestObjection: Large variance, no classifier value, vessels over a millimeter across, normal sites in symptomatic muscle.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Pain-free controls establishing the normal variation.
Microvascular Doppler in the muscle bed itself.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Retrograde diastolic flow at 15 of 48 (31%) palpably normal sites (VASO-E022), which the source cannot separate from spillover because no pain-free group was examined (VASO-E026).

treatment.plainLanguage: About a third of the 'normal' sites in these patients also showed backward flow between heartbeats.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: It caps the Doppler finding: the waveform is a gradient across symptomatic muscle, not a marker of a knot.
treatment.strongestObjection: The normal sites lay five centimeters from a trigger point in the same muscle; a true baseline rate is unknown.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A pain-free baseline rate for retrograde flow in the trapezius.
Doppler at sites fixed by instrument rather than palpation.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Both means are quoted from the paper's results (VASO-E087 for the active value, VASO-E089 for the latent value), with the active-versus-latent significance and classifier (VASO-E093, VASO-E106) as context and the calf area difference (VASO-E085) as a parallel from another muscle and method. Blinded sonographers, one laboratory, one vibration frequency, palpation-selected sites.

treatment.plainLanguage: On vibration elastography, active trigger points cover a larger stiff area than latent ones — about 0.57 against 0.36 square centimeters.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Graded stiffness with symptom severity is what every account predicts.
treatment.strongestObjection: A single vibration frequency from an off-the-shelf massager, shear elasticity not measured, and the contrast presupposes the palpated classification.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Replication with shear-wave elastography in a second laboratory.
Failure to replicate the ordering at instrument-fixed sites.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The value is quoted from the paper's results with the P<.01 across site types (VASO-E090); the ROC records VASO-E104, VASO-E105 and VASO-E107 are attached but read by the second reader as context toward this descriptive figure. The 'normal' sites were palpably normal sites in symptomatic patients, at least five centimeters from a trigger point.

treatment.plainLanguage: Palpably normal sites in the same symptomatic muscles showed a stiff area of about 0.17 square centimeters, smaller than either class of trigger point.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Completes the active-above-latent-above-normal gradient; the gradient itself is predicted by all accounts.
treatment.strongestObjection: No pain-free tissue was measured, so the value is not a normal baseline.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Elastography at matched sites in pain-free controls.
A replication in which normal-site areas overlap the latent range.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Endplate noise at four of eleven non-tender endplate-zone sites outside any trigger point, P=0.024 (VASO-E032), in a nonrandomized, unblinded study of ten subjects by the construct's leading proponents.

treatment.plainLanguage: The electrical hum also turns up at some non-tender spots, so long as they lie in the muscle's nerve-supply zone.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Cuts against the nidus being exclusive to trigger points and places the signature in the endplate zone first.
treatment.strongestObjection: Abstract only, small, unblinded.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A blinded replication with per-site amplitudes.
A repeat finding no endplate noise at non-tender endplate-zone sites.

claimAssessments.reasoning: No endplate noise at taut-band sites outside the endplate zone, P=0.000034 (VASO-E032), same small unblinded study.

treatment.plainLanguage: Tight bands of muscle outside the nerve-supply zone show no such electrical hum.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Ties the signature to skeletal-muscle endplates rather than to any tissue that happens to be taut.
treatment.strongestObjection: Abstract only, small, unblinded, proponent authors.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A blinded replication.
Spontaneous activity recorded at off-zone taut bands.

claimAssessments.reasoning: No differences in resistivity index between active, latent and normal sites, and the pulsatility index did not classify sites (VASO-E024). Within-patient comparison in symptomatic muscle.

treatment.plainLanguage: A second measure of downstream vascular resistance showed no difference between trigger points and normal sites.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A null that keeps the vascular footprint partial rather than categorical.
treatment.strongestObjection: Proximity of normal sites to trigger points may have masked a difference.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Pain-free controls showing a resistivity difference.
Microvascular Doppler in the bed itself rather than conduit arteries.
